newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Prices fall with quality at Colombo Rubber auction.
newsitem.headline: Prices fall with quality at Colombo Rubber auction.

text.p: Crepe prices were slightly down at the Colombo auction on Thursday due to a drop in quality stemming from heavy rain in tapping areas, brokers said.
"The market was active for all grades, but prices were down as quality rubber was not available," said Upali Bandaranayake of brokers Forbes & Walker.
Heavy rain, which has been lashing the countryside, has affected quality and quantities at the auction, brokers said. Rain prevents rubber tapping and lowers latex quality.
Best latex one-x, the purest grade, which went unquoted on Tuesday when the auction was last held, fetched 72.50 per kilo.
RSS 1 was 63.52 and also was unquoted on Tuesday. Crepe number one dropped slightly to 71 rupees from 71.75 on Tuesday.
On Thursday, the auction offered 235 tonnes of latex and scrap rubber.
Bandaranayake said a further drop in quality was anticipated at next week's auction as rains showed no sign of abating.
"There is demand for good rubber," he said.
Another broker said demand would be gradually dropping as the holiday season approached and overseas buyers began to go on leave.
